problem: Vision-based object navigation models (end-to-end and BEV semantic-map) cannot reliably perceive obstacles such as tables and walls, because obstacles may be missing from the image or missed by detectors. Agents then repeat 'MoveAhead' and get stuck in a local area.
motivation: Obstacle avoidance is critical for successful goal-driven indoor navigation, and image-based obstacle perception is fragile. Whether a forward move changes the agent's coordinates directly reveals whether a direction is passable, without relying on vision. The agent also needs to keep track of the target's orientation to choose sensible rotations when avoiding obstacles.
key_idea: Build an implicit obstacle map from trial-and-error feedback (whether forward motion changed the agent's coordinates) in 8 directions, and fuse it with a non-local cross-attention aggregation of target-orientation memory in an A3C-trained LSTM policy.
insight: Obstacle information from motion outcomes is more robust than image cues or sparse grid maps. In the AI2-Thor ablation, IOM alone raises SR from 78.51 to 81.04, and it beats the tentative policy network (TPN, 79.63) and a grid map (GM, 76.07). Attention-based target memory aggregation outperforms averaging and multi-scale conv aggregation (TAMSA), and its weights favor recent features. The new reward alone does nothing (SR 78.72) but amplifies IOM and NTWA together (SR 82.99).
method: Implicit obstacle map (IOM): for 8 directions (45° apart) a vector z_t holds -1 (coordinates unchanged after forward, impassable), 1 (passable) or 0 (unknown). It is concatenated with the (x,y) coordinates into m_t (1x10), and a fixed-size memory of e entries keeps the closest previous entries.
IOM encoder: two linear layers with ReLU (10->32, then compress along the memory dimension) give the 1x32 obstacle embedding M_t.
Target memory: target orientation feature D_t (DETR target bbox+confidence, plus pose x, y, yaw, pitch; 9-d) is accumulated up to length tau, dropping the entry farthest from the current one.

Non-local target memory aggregation (NTWA): the target semantic (one-hot mapped by an MLP, concatenated with pose) is the query, and the MLP-lifted memory is key/value. Multi-head cross-attention (4 heads, dropout 0.1) gives F_t (1x32).
State and policy: s_t = concat(ResNet image feature, weighted DETR object feature, M_t, F_t) W_a, fed to an LSTM policy trained with A3C after supervised action-label pre-training.
Reward: per-step -0.01; +0.01 for moving forward when the target is not found; +0.01 when distance to the found target decreases; -0.01 for collision; +0.02 for avoiding an obstacle; +5 for success.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + DETR features + MLP/attention modules + LSTM policy (trained with A3C)
setting.training_data: Imitation pre-training on action labels, then RL for 3M episodes on AI2-Thor / RoboTHOR training scenes (14 workers, 2 RTX 2080Ti)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image, plus agent pose/coordinates (x, y, yaw, pitch) and detector outputs
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookDown, LookUp, Done
setting.privileged: agent coordinates from the simulator (used to detect collisions and to build the map); no GT map

results: The full model reaches SR/SPL/SAE of 82.99/47.40/33.04 on AI2-Thor and 42.07/27.47/24.42 on RoboTHOR. It beats the strongest baseline, DAT (80.95/39.82 SR), by 2.04/2.25 SR, and the semantic-map method PONI (79.64/38.73) by 3.35/3.34. Episode time is 0.38/1.35 s, far below the map-based methods.
limitations: Relies on exact agent coordinates from the simulator to detect collisions and would need reliable odometry in the real world; only evaluated in simulation.
The reward mechanism is only useful together with IOM and NTWA; SPL gains are small, and RoboTHOR success rates remain low (~42%).
